authoredFrom: SOL-6 — nothing is emitted from a recovery region, and a recovery region is a RANGE OF SOURCE LINES, not an ERROR node's subtree. Authored 2026-09-30 from the analyzer's measured output, and this fixture exists because writing it FOUND the rule too narrow.
note: The pinned corpus is 0% damaged over all 389 production files, so a corpus run cannot exercise this rule at all. That is exactly why the rule needs a fixture that forces an ERROR on purpose: the first version of SOL-6 skipped an ERROR node's DESCENDANTS, and on this file the parser emits `ERROR` covering only `is not ) valid solidity ( at` with a MISSING `;` — so the tokens `this` and `all` are SIBLINGS of the ERROR node, outside its subtree, and the subtree rule published a symbol named `all` and a type reference `this`. What the parser cannot recover is the LINE, so the rule is now a pre-pass over ERROR/MISSING line spans consulted by both emit helpers.

forbidSymbols.name: all
forbidSymbols.comment: THE ROW THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR. `all` is the last token of the unparseable line. It is a SIBLING of the ERROR node, not a descendant, so a subtree-skipping rule let it through and published a symbol for a token the parser invented. A graph is not the place to store a guess.

expectRelationships.comment: A clean declaration on line 6 SURVIVES even though line 7 is a recovery line. The rule is per-LINE, not per-FILE: refusing the whole file because one line is broken would throw away real facts, which is the opposite error.
Line 8 is AFTER the recovery line and is emitted normally.

forbidRelationships.comment: The same fact as forbidSymbols, pinned as an EDGE: the parser's guess must not become a containment edge either. Symbols and relationships are refused by two different helpers, so both need their own row — a rule that suppressed one and not the other would pass half this fixture.

MEASURED on the pre-fix analyzer: `uses -> this` with `isTypeReference: true` on the recovery line, from a recovery fragment that parsed as a type mention. Two independent defects met on one line — the recovery rule was too narrow, AND the user_defined_type branch did not exclude the EVM globals the way the read branch does. Both are fixed and both are pinned.
Same recovery line, seen as a declaration.
